summary: A web platform that enables NASA to compare the topographic and thermal characteristics of the Moon and Earth to identify potential terrestrial analog sites for testing and evaluation through 3D simulations of terrain and surface temperature. In addition, it integrates logistical planning and cost estimation tools, along with a reservation system that allows space agencies, space stations, and private companies to manage access to selected sites for conducting their experiments. Ultimately, the platform aims to reduce uncertainty in test-site selection, optimize available resources, and lower the costs associated with the development and validation of technologies for future lunar and Martian missions.
details:
The platform will provide NASA with a dedicated user profile through which it can access 3D simulations of lunar and Martian terrain locations, as well as estimate the logistical costs of transporting equipment from different space stations or private companies to selected sites for testing and evaluation. External users will also be able to access the platform to compare terrestrial analog sites, view the similarity percentage between the characteristics of the Moon and Mars and those of different regions on Earth, and request logistical cost estimates for transporting their equipment to the selected locations. This will help optimize resources and reduce costs associated with the preparation and execution of future lunar and Martian missions.

The platform was developed using React 19 and TypeScript for the frontend, together with Vite 8 and Bun 1.3 for building, execution, and dependency installation. 3D visualization was implemented using Three.js, while mapping functionalities were developed with MapLibre GL and world-atlas. The backend was built with Python and FastAPI, using SQLAlchemy 2, psycopg 3, and PostgreSQL (Neon) for data management, along with httpx for communication with external services. Python, Rasterio, and NumPy were used to process geospatial and thermal information, while Google Earth Engine was used to query and export MODIS data. The platform also integrates artificial intelligence through Google Gemini (gemini-3.5-flash and gemini-flash-lite-latest), as well as several data sources and services, including NASA, NOAA, USGS, Copernicus, Open-Meteo, WorldClim, SoilGrids, and OpenStreetMap. Git and GitHub were used for version control and team collaboration, Postman for API testing, pytest and bun test for software testing, and Oxlint for code analysis. Finally, the frontend was deployed using Vercel and the backend using Render.

The project's creative innovation lies in integrating virtual robots to simulate operations on lunar and Martian analog terrains through 3D visualization, together with tools for estimating the logistical costs of transporting the equipment required to conduct tests at these locations. This makes it possible to visualize potential operational scenarios, compare alternatives, and anticipate resource requirements before conducting physical tests, supporting decision-making and more efficient planning for future space missions.

To identify terrestrial sites with the greatest similarity to lunar and Martian surfaces, the team uses three main variables in the similarity calculation: elevation, slope, and terrain roughness. Additionally, the platform provides comparative thermal information, including daytime and nighttime surface temperatures and their variation between these periods. It also incorporates complementary data on solar radiation, soil type, and granulometry, as well as AI-based estimates of rock abundance derived from photographs of terrestrial sites. These factors provide a broader characterization of each location and additional information for assessing its potential as a terrestrial analog site.
